title: KV prefetch ops check-in (2027-02-23)
content:
Summary:
- Quick mid-week capture from the applied-ml kv-prefetch / quantization sync (Feb 23). Focus: reduce per-host memory + token-latency for 13B-class open models while keeping eval/regression risk low. This is an operational + evaluation checkpoint rather than final decisions.

Attendees:
- Aisha (owner), Ethan (bench + infra), Ravi (quant research), Claire (evals), Marta (onboarding).

Meeting notes / decisions:
- We validated two promising knobs: a) nf4-style 4-bit per-channel symmetric quant (WIP) with scaled zeros, b) light-weight prefetching of KV shards during warm-starts (prefetch window 128->512 tokens).
- Short-circuit: NF4-per-channel + prefetch=ON gives best memory/latency trade in local bench. Still need behavioral eval sweep.
- Agreed to gate rollout on: decoder perplexity delta <= +1.0 on Evals-v2 dev prompts, top-level fallback if embedding cosine < 0.985 vs baseline, and no increase in harmful-completion alerts in safety suite.

Experiment log (raw):
- experiment: nf4-per-channel + symmetric scaling; model: open-13B-v2 (float baseline)
  - tokens/testset: 3.2M prompt tokens (Evals-v2 subset)
  - perplexity: baseline 12.4 -> quant 12.9 (+0.5)
  - embedding-cosine (anchor set): 0.998 -> 0.995 (-0.003)
  - memory: host GPU resident 43GB -> 12.6GB (model + KV cache)
  - avg token latency (p50, tok=1): 41.8ms -> 27.3ms
  - throughput (batch 4): 1.0x -> 1.68x
  - notes: a handful of long-tail tokenization edge cases triggered slightly different completions for date-format prompts (ticketed ML-8190).

- experiment: dynamic-range-rescale + 8-bit activations (hybrid)
  - perplexity change: +0.15 (better than nf4 on some tasks)
  - memory: 43GB -> 18.9GB
  - latency: 41.8ms -> 32.1ms
  - tradeoff: lower quality regression but simpler fallback path (can detour to hybrid variant).

Eval results (short):
- Evals-v2 (64 prompt set) overall pass rate: baseline 100% -> nf4 92% (failure modes mostly long-run arithmetic/format), hybrid 97%.
- Safety regression (toxicity heuristics + safety-LM probes): nf4 shows +0.4% alerts (small, investigate), hybrid +0.1%.
- Reranker/regression check: reranking MRR unchanged within noise.

Operational notes (onboarding + infra):
- Prefetch window increase (128->512) cuts cold-start tails but increases ephemeral memory during warm-up; when combined with nf4 memory is still < baseline so acceptable. Need autoscaler tweak to account for 512-window burst.
- KV-shard placement: Ethan to run microbench comparing stripe=2 vs stripe=4 for our Dedicated config; early bench favors stripe=2 for latency.
- Model packaging: new quantized artifacts are saved under artifact-store/qa/13b/nf4-perch-20270223.tar (internal bucket). Add checksum + version pin in model catalogue.

Key blockers / open questions:
- Which eval set is the canonical gating set for rollout? Claire recommends Evals-v2 + 2 long-tail suites (dates, code) — need sign-off from product-hosted-api.
- Safety false positives: which alerts are actionable vs noise? Need SRE/safety sign-off before canary.
- Runtime support: does private-deployments runtime have stable nf4 codepath? (item for infra-team).

Action items (owners):
- Ravi: run full regression sweep (Evals-v2 extended 5k prompts) + generate p95/p99 of metric deltas. Due: 2027-02-28. (JIRA ML-8202)
- Ethan: stripe microbench + autoscaler simulation with prefetch=512. Record tail-latency distribution. Due: 2027-03-02.
- Claire: curate canonical gating set + safety checklist; include 30 targeted prompts for date/code churn. Due: 2027-02-25.
- Marta: prepare onboarding checklist (packaging, model-catalog entry, rollout canary steps, rollback conditions). Draft to infra-runbook. Due: 2027-03-01.
- Aisha: coordinate product-hosted-api sign-off and schedule canary window (tentative week of Mar 7).

Notes-to-self / rough ideas:
- Consider ephemeral quant caches on CPU to accelerate initial KV load for prefetch window > 256 (cheap memory swap).
- If safety alerts persist, try constrained decoding tweak + temperature reduction during fallback.
- Potential follow-up: integrate quantization QA into CI (PR gate) to catch obvious perplexity regressions quickly.

Links & references:
- quant playbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Quantization+Playbook
- PR: https://github.com/redwood/kv-cache/pull/342
- Jira: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/ML-8123 (kv-prefetch opt), ML-8202 (regression sweep)
- artifact: s3://artifacts.redwood/qa/13b/nf4-perch-20270223.tar

Next sync: brief standup Tuesday Feb 28 — focus on regression sweep outputs and stripe microbench.

-- Aisha
